title: Dog-Trade Claims Need Proof, Quarantine, and Abolition by 2030
excerpt: A stolen companion and an infected animal create different harms. Both demand evidence, enforcement, quarantine, and a clear path to abolition by 2030.
body_html:
A dog bite can become fatal when rabies symptoms begin. The World Health Organization states that rabies is virtually 100% fatal after clinical symptoms appear. Wash any wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, then seek urgent medical care for vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. This immediate danger belongs in every discussion of animal movement and slaughter.

But evidence must govern the argument. Claims that Vietnam’s dog-meat supply relies entirely on stolen pets, or that no farm-raised dogs exist, require case records, seizure reports, transport documents, court judgments, and traceable veterinary evidence. None of those specific records, dates, locations, or named agencies appears in the material available for this dispatch. Fabrication would weaken victims, families, Vietnamese reformers, and public-health work.

Separate harms. Shared enforcement gap.

Pet theft is a direct assault on families. Illegal transport, missing quarantine controls, and uninspected slaughter raise separate biosecurity concerns. A household rabies exposure does not, by itself, prove a commercial supply-chain link. Nor does a trade claim prove disease transmission. Each allegation needs its own evidence, investigation, and accountability.

Tradition cannot replace traceability

Tradition does not excuse poison bait, theft, unlawful transport, or evasion of veterinary controls. Lawful activity, documented criminal conduct, regulatory breaches, and proposed abolition must remain distinct. Vietnam’s communities deserve safe streets, protected companion animals, transparent enforcement, and leadership that closes legal gaps rather than hiding them.

SDE calls for nationwide abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for action, then follow campaign updates as that demand reaches decision-makers.

Rabies control cannot stop at household gates. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. After a possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical care for vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies.

That public-health duty must stand beside another duty: protect families from stolen companion animals and illegal animal transport. These harms are connected by enforcement gaps, but they are not interchangeable proof. A household exposure does not establish a commercial supply-chain link. A claim about dog-meat sourcing does not establish disease transmission. Investigators need seizure records, court judgments, transport documents, quarantine records, and veterinary evidence.

Vietnamese communities deserve safe streets, protected pets, transparent enforcement, and reform led by people who know these harms firsthand. Tradition cannot excuse poison bait, theft, unlawful transport, or evasion of veterinary controls. SDE calls for nationwide abolition by 2030.
